statusNote: GSoC 2026 is in its project work phase.
summary: Google Summer of Code is a global, online program that brings new contributors into open source. Contributors work with an open source organization on a 12+ week programming project under the guidance of mentors.

stipend.detail: Paid by Google, adjusted for the contributor's country with Purchasing Power Parity (PPP). Base amounts are $1,500 for a small project, $3,000 for a medium project and $6,000 for a large project.
stipend.method: Payoneer, which serves 190+ countries. From 2026 Payoneer cannot pay account holders in Quebec, Canada.
stipend.tableNote: Amount for your country, by project size (GSoC 2026 table).

facts.label: Length
facts.value: 8 to 22 weeks; start dates are fixed, end dates can be extended up to 22 weeks

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Online, with mentors from the organization

facts.label: Proposals
facts.value: Up to three per contributor; only one can be accepted

eligibility: A student, or an open source beginner (for example, fewer than 10 pull requests to open source packages).
Eligible to work in your country of residence.
Accepted into GSoC no more than once before.
Not living in a U.S. embargoed country; people in Russia, Belarus and the DNR/LNR regions are currently not eligible.
howToApply: Pick organizations from the accepted list and read their project ideas.
Talk to the organization's mentors in their chat or mailing list before writing a proposal.
Submit up to three proposals on summerofcode.withgoogle.com before the proposal deadline.
Organizations rank proposals; accepted contributors are announced publicly.
